title: Factors Associated With the Autonomy of Patients Treated by Haemodialysis in Community Centres. A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: All patients receiving haemodialysis in community centres in a French region on December 31, 2021. MEASUREMENTS: Patient characteristics and multiple dimensions of patient autonomy were recorded. Multivariate analyses assessed associations between patient factors and technical autonomy. RESULTS: Among 507 patients, 304 were treated in self-care units and 203 in satellite haemodialysis units. Patients in satellite haemodialysis units had a median age of 69 years (IQR 59-78; range 24-90), compared with 66 years (IQR 54-75; range 22-91) in self-care haemodialysis units. They also had more comorbidities. Younger age was associated with greater autonomy in arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), setting the haemodialysis machine (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), and programming it (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Autonomy differed significantly between centres, with centre affiliation significantly associated (p < .001) with autonomy for the arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing and machine-related tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Patient characteristics in self-care haemodialysis units did not fully explain autonomy for haemodialysis tasks. Considerable variability between centres was observed, suggesting that centre-related factors may contribute to differences in patient autonomy.

Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units.

title: Maintaining IV Patency Throughout Pharmacokinetic Studies Through a Needle-Free Blood Draw Device.
abstract: 8 8 9 Pharmacokinetic (PK) studies require temporally precise measurements of drug concentrations in biological matrices, most commonly whole blood or plasma. However, repeated venous sampling may increase participant burden and complicate PK-intensive study designs. Needle-free blood collection devices that access peripheral intravenous (IV) catheters may provide an alternative approach to repeated venipuncture while maintaining sampling schedules and specimen quality. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of integrating the PIVO Pro needle-free blood collection device into a PK-intensive human laboratory study of inhaled Δ-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ-THC), Δ-THC, and placebo. Participants completed a screening visit and three dosing visits conducted in a university research facility equipped with a full-scale driving simulator. During each dosing visit, venous blood samples were collected at nine time points over approximately 8 h through an indwelling peripheral IV catheter using the PIVO device. All participants reported that study procedures, including blood collection, were acceptable. Approximately 40% of vascular access sites required replacement, most commonly within the first hour and typically associated with poor initial blood return. Despite slower flow compared with standard venipuncture, sampling was generally sufficient to maintain the PK sampling schedule. One mild adverse event related to vascular access (localized bruising) was observed. These findings demonstrate the operational feasibility of needle-free blood collection through indwelling IV catheters in a PK-intensive research protocol conducted outside a traditional clinical research unit. Further studies are warranted to compare analytical performance and access durability relative to conventional venous sampling approaches.

title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods. AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025. RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59). CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement. STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool. RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps. CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

title: [Abdominal aortic aneurysms: diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment strategies].
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as a focal aortic dilation ≥3.0 cm in maximum diameter, with rupture-associated mortality approaching 80%. Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women. Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) provides an early survival benefit, with 30-day mortality of 1.8% vs 4.3% for open repair in the EVAR-1 trial, and substantially comparable long-term outcomes up to 15 years of follow-up, at the cost of a 15-20% reintervention burden and the need for lifelong imaging surveillance. Accordingly, the 2024 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider EVAR as the preferred treatment in most patients with favorable anatomy, reserving open repair for young patients with long life expectancy, unfavorable anatomy and specific conditions such as connective tissue disease, inflammatory aneurysms, graft infection and failed previous endovascular repair. Treatment selection should be based on the integrated assessment of individual operative risk, aortic anatomy and life expectancy.

Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.

title: Delayed and prolonged hypotension and watershed cerebral infarction following coil embolization of an extracranial carotid artery aneurysm: A possible baroreceptor-mediated complication.
abstract: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare vascular lesions increasingly treated by endovascular approaches when open repair is unfavorable. Although hemodynamic depression related to carotid baroreceptor activation is recognized during carotid interventions, delayed and prolonged hypotension after primary coil embolization of an ECAA is rarely reported. A 64-year-old man underwent primary coil embolization for an enlarging high cervical ECAA because severe proximal internal carotid artery tortuosity precluded safe stent reconstruction. After an initially uneventful recovery, progressive hypotension developed approximately 1-2 hours after the procedure and ultimately required vasopressor support through postoperative day 16. Recurrent hypotension was followed by acute neurological deterioration. Computed tomography angiography showed no large-vessel occlusion, aneurysm rupture, or overt parent artery compromise, whereas diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a left watershed infarction consistent with hypoperfusion. Blood pressure augmentation resulted in rapid neurological recovery. Because the aneurysm was adjacent to the carotid bulb, carotid baroreceptor activation related to post-embolization geometric change was considered a possible mechanism. This case highlights the need for careful hemodynamic monitoring after coil embolization of ECAAs near the carotid bulb, even without balloon angioplasty or stent deployment.

title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: High-intensity focused ultrasound as a bridging vascular-modulating therapy for fertility-sparing management of placental site trophoblastic tumor complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) is a rare gestational trophoblastic neoplasm characterized by local invasiveness and marked vascularity. Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases. CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old woman presented with persistently plateaued serum human chorionic gonadotropin levels following hysteroscopic management for suspected incomplete abortion. Imaging revealed a deeply invasive hypervascular uterine lesion with UAVF, raising strong suspicion of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Given her strong desire for fertility preservation and high surgical risk, ultrasound-guided HIFU was performed as an initial vascular-modulating intervention. Subsequent expert pathological review confirmed PSTT. RESULTS: HIFU achieved significant reduction in lesion perfusion and vascular flow, as confirmed by Doppler ultrasound and contrast-enhanced MRI. Although complete tumor ablation was not achieved due to lesion size and deep invasion, subsequent low-dose chemotherapy resulted in complete biochemical remission accompanied by radiologic regression of residual lesions. No major HIFU-related complications were observed, and normal menstrual function resumed during follow-up. CONCLUSION: HIFU is a technically feasible and safe fertility-preserving adjunct for vascular modulation in hypervascular PSTT complicated by UAVF. While HIFU alone may not achieve definitive oncologic control in large or deeply invasive lesions, it can serve as a bridging strategy to reduce tumor perfusion and vascularity, facilitating subsequent systemic therapy in carefully selected patients. This approach demonstrates the potential role of HIFU as a bridging vascular-modulating strategy within multimodal fertility-preserving management.

Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases.

title: Pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia are associated with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cohort study from Gaza.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 poses significant risks to pregnant women, with pregnancy recognized as a risk factor for severe disease. This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function. METHODS: n n A retrospective cohort study of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19 was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza (2021). Pregnant ( = 97) and nonpregnant ( = 174) groups were stratified by IDA, investigating the impact of pregnancy and IDA on the severity of COVID-19. Iron deficiency was determined by transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection, whereas ferritin levels were not available. RESULTS: p p p p p p p p Overall pregnancy was significantly associated with COVID-19 severity ( < 0.001), with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. All deaths were due to acute respiratory distress syndrome; no venous thromboembolism cases occurred. IDA was associated with COVID-19 severity in both pregnant ( = 0.015) and non-pregnant ( = 0.002) women. In a multivariable model including pregnancy, IDA was associated with higher odds of severe (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.97-6.48, < 0.001), critical (OR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.09-4.64, = 0.029), and fatal illness (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 1.96-26.74, = 0.003) compared with moderate illness. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that among young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women with COVID-19, pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. However, interpretation requires caution considering the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the assessment of iron status during acute infection using transferrin saturation alone without ferritin measurements, which limits the ability to distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes in iron metabolism.

This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function. title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis.

title: Nurse-led, multidisciplinary strategies to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections: Parenteral nutrition stewardship and central venous access device maintenance.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs) remain a major source of preventable patient harm and are associated with increased mortality, longer hospital stays, and higher health care costs. Reducing central venous access device (CVAD) utilization and improving line maintenance practices are key strategies for prevention. PURPOSE: To reduce CLABSIs through a nurse-led, multidisciplinary initiative focused on parenteral nutrition (PN) stewardship, CVAD maintenance, and shared accountability for line necessity and care. METHODS: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, an interprofessional team implemented a PN clinical decision tree, standardized PN administration kit, targeted nursing education, daily multidisciplinary line rounds, and real-time escalation processes. Outcomes included CLABSI Standardized Infection Ratio (SIR), Standardized Utilization Ratio (SUR), PN-related CLABSIs, and adherence to line care practices. RESULTS: The initiative was associated with a 46% reduction in CLABSI SIR (1.165-0.632), an 11.7% reduction in CVAD utilization (SUR 0.479-0.423; P < .001), and a decrease in PN-related CLABSIs from 45% to 12.5% of all CLABSI cases. Process-related issues identified during rounds decreased from 32.73% to 26.11%. CONCLUSIONS: A nurse-led, multidisciplinary approach combining PN stewardship, standardized CVAD care, and real-time feedback improved patient safety and reduced CLABSI risk. The model offers a sustainable, replicable strategy for infection prevention.

PURPOSE: To reduce CLABSIs through a nurse-led, multidisciplinary initiative focused on parenteral nutrition (PN) stewardship, CVAD maintenance, and shared accountability for line necessity and care.

title: Clinical outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair by in situ microneedle fenestration using the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.
abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair (TEAAR) via in situ micro-needle fenestration (ISMNF) with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment. This configuration creates a gutter between the stent-graft and aortic wall to maintain perfusion to supra-aortic branches. Operative details, technical success, 30-day and midterm outcomes, and adverse events were recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate freedom from all-cause death and reintervention. RESULTS: Overall, 36 patients were included. The technical success rate was 94.4% (34/36). Endovascular reconstruction of cervical branches was successfully performed in all cases. The 30-day mortality was 2.8%. The median follow-up period was 19 months (range, 1-32 months). The all-cause death rate was 11.1% (4/36), with no cases of any aorta-related death. The prevalence of endoleaks during follow-up was 13.9% (5/36). The overall stroke rate was 8.3% (3/36). The 1- and 2-year survival rates were 97.3% ± 2.7% and 85.8% ± 8.1%, respectively. The cumulative rate of freedom from reintervention at 1 and 2 years was 87.5% ± 5.9% and 83.2% ± 7.0%, respectively. CONCLUSION: TEAAR via ISMNF with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique was performed with a 94% technical success rate and stroke risk similar to open surgery.

title: Characteristics of treatment responses to physical exercise and diet in diabetic peripheral artery disease patients: a systematic review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects walking performance and increases risk of amputation. Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only contributes to disease progression but may also affect treatment effects. Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear. The present systematic review aims to summarize features of treatment response to physical exercise and diet management in diabetic PAD patients, and provide crucial information on optimization of PAD management of these patients in clinical practice. METHODS: A systematic review was performed on human studies investigating effects of physical exercise and diet on development and improvement of diabetic PAD patients by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL. The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA). The certainty level of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: A total of 18 studies were included, 15 of which evaluated effects of exercise on diabetic PAD, and three evaluated correlation between diet and diabetic PAD. Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and home-based exercise were able to improve ankle-brachial index (ABI) and blood flow velocity in diabetic PAD. In contrast, walking performance such as the six minute walk distance (6MWD), maximal walking time and distance, peak walking time (PWT) and claudication onset time (COT) were not significantly improved or presented conflicting results. Administration of multiple exercises or alternative interventions such as shock wave therapy or low-frequency pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (LFPMT) may enhance improvement of ABI. Adherence to Mediterranean diet was associated with blood flow and intermittent claudication, as well as risk of development of PAD. GRADE analysis revealed very low to moderate grade evidence for findings on ABI, flow velocity and functions, mainly due to study types, number of studies available, small sample size, moderate risk of bias and conflicting results. Similarly, low grade evidence was also revealed for effects and association of diet on risk of PAD due to study type and number of studies available. CONCLUSION: Diabetic PAD patients may present reduced treatment response to physical exercise in walking performance and other functions, which may be improved by combination of multiple physical exercises or alternative interventions with or without combination of exercise. Mediterranean diet may be associated with beneficial effects, which requires further investigations. These findings were of very low to moderate level of certainty, and therefore, further validation is warranted in the future.

Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear.

title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

title: Association of modified cardiovascular health with long-term all-cause mortality among adults with Ankle-Brachial Index-defined peripheral artery disease: a NHANES 1999-2004 cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether an integrated cardiovascular health profile is associated with long-term mortality among adults with objectively defined peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains insufficiently characterized in nationally representative cohorts. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥40 years with Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurements and linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019. PAD was defined as a minimum ABI ≤0.90. Modified cardiovascular health (mCVH; range 0-12) was constructed from smoking, Body Mass Index, physical activity, blood pressure, total cholesterol, and glycemic status. Corrected six-year Mobile Examination Center weights and complex survey design variables were used. Weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality using sequential adjustment for demographic factors, socioeconomic factors, survey cycle, and minimum ABI. Additional analyses evaluated non-PAD participants and cardiovascular mortality. RESULTS: The primary PAD cohort included 554 adults, among whom 428 deaths occurred during a median follow-up of 123.5 months. PAD participants had a higher absolute all-cause mortality burden than non-PAD participants. Each 1-point higher mCVH score was associated with lower all-cause mortality in Model 1 (HR 0.888, 95% CI 0.842-0.937; P<0.001), Model 2 (HR 0.922, 95% CI 0.870-0.977; P=0.006), and Model 3 (HR 0.926, 95% CI 0.874-0.982; P=0.010). Among non-PAD participants, higher mCVH was also associated with lower all-cause mortality, and the mCVH × PAD status interaction was not statistically significant (P=0.122). In sensitivity analysis, higher mCVH was also associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.863, 95% CI 0.786-0.948; P=0.002). Component-level analyses suggested that smoking was the most robust individual component. CONCLUSIONS: Among U.S. adults with ABI-defined PAD, higher baseline mCVH was associated with lower long-term all-cause mortality. These findings support the prognostic relevance of integrated cardiovascular health profiling after objective PAD identification, while highlighting smoking as the most consistent individual component.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥40 years with Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurements and linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019. PAD was defined as a minimum ABI ≤0.90.

title: Trough Rivaroxaban Plasma Concentrations and Early Thrombus Regression in Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Sub-analysis of the SAKURA-PE/DVT REGISTRY.
abstract: Objectives　To evaluate the association between trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations and early thrombus regression in patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE).Methods　This study was a sub-analysis of the multicenter, prospective SAKURA PE/DVT REGISTRY. The thrombus regression rate was calculated using contrast-enhanced computed tomography performed at diagnosis and approximately two weeks after treatment initiation. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were measured using a chromogenic anti-factor Xa assay. Correlations between plasma concentrations, thrombus regression rates, and coagulation parameters were analyzed.Patients　Among 153 patients with acute PE treated with direct oral anticoagulants, 106 received rivaroxaban, and trough plasma concentrations were measured in 51 patients.Results　The median trough rivaroxaban plasma concentration was 120.0 (55.6-186.0) ng/mL, with substantial interindividual variability. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were positively correlated with the thrombus regression rate in all patients (ρ = 0.33, P = 0.018) and in the intensive therapy group (ρ = 0.41, P = 0.009). In the multivariable analysis, log-transformed rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were independently associated with the thrombus regression rate in the intensive therapy group (β = 9.79, 95% confidence interval 0.72-18.86; P = 0.035). Prothrombin time was strongly correlated with rivaroxaban plasma concentration (ρ = 0.85, P < 0.001). Plasma concentrations tended to increase with age and showed greater variability in elderly patients.Conclusion　Higher trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were associated with greater early thrombus regression in patients with acute PE. Prothrombin time may be a practical surrogate for rivaroxaban exposure and may support individualized anticoagulation strategies in selected patients.

title: Recurrent Ischemic Stroke after Carotid Artery Stenting for Thyroid Cartilage Induced CCA Stenosis: Was Stenting an Appropriate Treatment?
abstract: Mechanical stimulation of the common carotid artery (CCA) by the hyoid bone or thyroid cartilage can cause common carotid artery (CCA) stenosis and cerebral infarction. A 71-year-old man presented with symptomatic CCA stenosis. Imaging revealed CCA plaque at the site of contact with the thyroid cartilage, and ultrasonography revealed dynamic compression during swallowing. Despite technically successful carotid artery stenting, infarctions can recur without typical stent-related complications. The plaque may be trapped by the stent under persistent external mechanical stress, resulting in intermittent protrusions. Additional stenting prevented the recurrence. This case highlights the importance of considering external mechanical factors when selecting a treatment strategy.

title: in vivo Continuous site-specific intravascular monitoring of arterial and venous blood oxygenation.
abstract: Objective Approach. n Main results. Significance. . Conventional pulse oximetry (PO) provides continuous noninvasive arterial oxygen saturation, whereas arterial and venous blood gas analysis provides intermittent reference measurements. Neither modality continuously monitors saturation at a selected deep intravascular site. In this proof-of-concept feasibility study, we assessed whether intravascular diffuse reflectance spectroscopy tracks the direction and time course of prespecified arterial, central venous, and regional renal venous oxygenation changes, alongside conventional PO where an arterial comparator was appropriate.Three separate experimental protocols were performed in three pigs (one animal per protocol;= 1 per condition). Oxygen saturation was monitored with the iBLOS sensing wire in the abdominal aorta during apnea-induced systemic hypoxemia, in the inferior vena cava (IVC) during repeated hypoxic challenges, and in the right renal vein during transient venous outflow obstruction. Conventional PO was recorded concurrently during the arterial and IVC protocols as an arterial monitoring comparator; no blood-gas samples were collected in these feasibility experiments.Continuous intravascular blood oxygenation level monitoring detected rapid and dynamic arterial desaturation and reoxygenation during systemic apnea and demonstrated reproducible responses during repeated hypoxic challenges. Venous oxygenation measured in the IVC exhibited lower baseline oxygen saturation and slower desaturation-recovery kinetics than arterial measurements, reflecting physiological oxygen extraction and circulatory transit delays. During renal vein occlusion, oxygen saturation proximal to the obstruction progressively decreased toward near-complete oxygen depletion before rapidly recovering following restoration of venous outflow. These regional physiological measurements are not feasible using peripheral PO.This feasibility platform provides continuous, site-specific intravascular saturation trends in vascular territories that conventional noninvasive monitoring cannot directly sample. With validation against contemporaneous blood-gas measurements and evaluation in larger studies, it could help fill a monitoring gap during ischemia, reperfusion, and endovascular intervention.

title: Inflammation and thrombosis: from pathophysiology to future treatments.
abstract: Inflammation and coagulation are tightly interconnected host-defense systems that, when dysregulated, promote pathological thrombosis. This narrative review examines mechanisms, clinical settings, and therapeutic implications of thromboinflammation (TI) across venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, with particular attention to the differences in clinical translation among vascular territories. Endothelial activation, tissue factor expression, platelet-leukocyte interactions, neutrophil extracellular traps, complement activation, inflammasome signalling, and impaired fibrinolysis converge to generate a procoagulant phenotype. These mechanisms modify Virchow's triad and contribute to venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, although their relative importance varies across vascular territories. Clinically, TI is relevant in inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatologic and other immune-mediated disorders, sepsis, coronavirus disease 2019, clonal haematopoiesis, complement-mediated diseases, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. TI offers a unifying framework for mechanistic risk assessment and therapeutic development. In atherothrombosis, randomised trials have demonstrated that selective modulation of inflammatory pathways, particularly the NLRP3-interleukin-1β-interleukin-6 axis and colchicine-sensitive pathways, can reduce recurrent cardiovascular events. By contrast, the role of inflammation-targeted therapies for primary or secondary prevention of VTE remains uncertain. Future studies should identify disease-specific biomarkers and test targeted anti-inflammatory or immunothrombotic strategies, alone or alongside anticoagulation, to prevent thrombosis without compromising haemostasis effectively.

title: Pseudodominant inheritance in paraplegin (SPG7)-associated CPEO-ataxia syndrome.
abstract: SPG7 encodes paraplegin, a mitochondrial AAA-metalloprotease critical for inner mitochondrial membrane protein quality control. Pathogenic variants most commonly cause autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) but its phenotypic spectrum includes cerebellar ataxia, progressive external ophthalmoplegia, myopathy and parkinsonism.We report a 47 year old man presenting with a progressive external ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, progressive gait disturbance, and spasticity. Ten-year follow-up of this individual showed slowly progressive spastic ataxia with ocular motor involvement and neurogenic bladder. His mother and maternal aunt both had marked spasticity, ataxia, ptosis and external ophthalmoplegia. Genetic testing demonstrated compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in paraplegin in this individual. Genetic testing in his mother and aunt revealed homozygous canonical splice-site variants (c.2182-2 A > G). Cascade testing of his asymptomatic father showed a common pathogenic missense variant p.(Ala510Val) in the same gene.This family demonstrates a pseudodominant inheritance pattern, instead of the expected autosomal recessive trait that applies to paraplegin. We highlight diagnostic pitfalls in relying on family history and assumed inheritance traits. We emphasise the importance of segregation analysis and comprehensive genomic testing. Recognition of pseudodominance inheritance has important implications for genetic counselling, family planning and cascade testing.

title: Hemorrhagic Vocal Fold Inflammation Following Endotracheal Intubation in a Patient Undergoing Endovascular Neurosurgery Under Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic vocal fold inflammation is an uncommon complication of endotracheal intubation. Its clinical course in patients receiving perioperative antithrombotic therapy remains unclear. CASE PRESENTATION: A woman in her 60 s receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) underwent endovascular neurosurgery with flow-diverter stent deployment and coil embolization. Endotracheal intubation was uneventful, and cuff pressure was appropriately maintained. Hoarseness developed on postoperative day 1, and laryngoscopy on day 2 revealed hemorrhagic vocal fold inflammation. Intraoperative fluoroscopic images suggested proximal migration of the endotracheal tube, with possible changes in tube and cuff position that may have contributed to minor vocal fold mucosal injury. The symptoms improved with conservative management, and complete recovery was confirmed at 1 month. DISCUSSION: Hemorrhagic vocal fold inflammation occurred following apparently uneventful endotracheal intubation in a patient receiving perioperative antithrombotic therapy. Although the underlying mechanism remains uncertain, changes in endotracheal tube and cuff position during the procedure represent one possible contributing factor.

title: Maternal Obesity Is Associated With Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Matched Electronic Health Record Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We sought to define the prevalence of obesity in the first trimester of pregnancy among women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and evaluate its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes. METHODS: First-trimester body mass index (BMI) was assessed in pregnancies with and without IBD. Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk. RESULTS: Overall, 22.6% (64/283; 95% CI 17.7%-27.5%) of pregnancies in women with IBD met ethnicity-adjusted criteria for obesity. Increasing obesity class was associated with stepwise increases in gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, venous thromboembolism (VTE), emergency caesarean section and high birthweight. Matching yielded 177 IBD pregnancies and 1062 controls. Obesity was independently associated with the composite adverse pregnancy outcome (OR 1.63; 95% CI 1.15-2.33; p = 0.007), whereas no statistically significant additional association was identified for IBD diagnosis alone (OR 0.74; 95% CI 0.53-1.03; p = 0.073). Among IBD pregnancies, aspirin was recommended in 39.3% (86/219). Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) was prescribed in 21.6% (19/88) of pregnancies classified post hoc as intermediate or high VTE risk. CONCLUSION: More than one in five pregnancies in women with IBD were complicated by obesity. Obesity was strongly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas this study did not identify a significant additional effect attributable to IBD diagnosis alone. Preventive prescribing with aspirin and LMWH represents an opportunity for improved antenatal care.

METHODS: First-trimester body mass index (BMI) was assessed in pregnancies with and without IBD. Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk.

title: Doppler Ultrasonography and Computed Tomography Angiography in Carotid Artery Stenosis: Discordance and Its Potential Impact on Surgical Decision-Making.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The degree of carotid artery stenosis influences surgical decision-making; therefore, accurate assessment is essential for appropriate patient selection. This study evaluated agreement between Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) and computed tomography angiography (CTA) in patients with significant stenosis detected on DUS and investigated factors associated with discordance. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 79 patients who underwent DUS between January 2024 and October 2025 were included. DUS stenosis grade, CTA stenosis according to NASCET and ECST methods, lumen diameters, plaque characteristics, and accompanying vascular features were evaluated. RESULTS: Agreement between DUS and CTA was fair using NASCET (κ = 0.413; p < .001) and moderate using ECST (κ = 0.531; p < .001). Agreement between NASCET and ECST was substantial (κ = 0.799; p < .001). Discordance was most frequent in the 50-69% DUS stenosis group and varied according to stenosis severity and CTA measurement method. Plaque type, plaque length, and calcification were not associated with discordance. Residual lumen diameter on CTA was significantly larger in NASCET-based discordant cases (p = .018) whereas no significant difference was observed using ECST classification. In some patients, discrepancies could potentially affect surgical decision-making. CONCLUSION: Agreement between DUS and CTA in significant carotid stenosis was fair using NASCET and moderate using ECST, with discordance particularly frequent in the 50-69% stenosis group and dependent on the CTA measurement method. Combined assessment with 2 noninvasive imaging modalities may help reduce misclassification in patients considered for surgical treatment.

This study evaluated agreement between Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) and computed tomography angiography (CTA) in patients with significant stenosis detected on DUS and investigated factors associated with discordance. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 79 patients who underwent DUS between January 2024 and October 2025 were included.

title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults With Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: A NHANES Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90. A NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up ten steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment. RESULTS: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (OR 1.748, 95% CI 1.218-2.510; P=0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P=0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P=0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P=0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability. CONCLUSIONS: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90.

title: Common Femoral Atherectomy yields safe results and low morbidity in the outpatient setting.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy is considered the gold standard for the treatment of CFA disease. Some patients with CFA occlusive disease have significant comorbidities that may prevent them from undergoing open surgery. Several endovascular treatment options for the CFA, such as atherectomy, angioplasty, and stenting, are available but have not been widely adopted. This study aimed to describe our experience expanding the use of atherectomy in the outpatient setting for the treatment of CFA disease. METHODS: This is a single-institution, retrospective review of 49 CFA atherectomy procedures performed from January 2017 to November 2022 at Trinity Health Ann Arbor. Primary outcomes included primary patency at 1 year and MALE-free survival. Secondary outcomes involved changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI), toe pressures, and morbidity at 90 days. RESULTS: 49 CFA atherectomies were performed on 45 patients (73 yo ± 7 years), 45% with claudication and 55% with critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). TASC classification of the treated lesions was TASC A in 4%, TASC B in 29%, TASC C in 61%, and TASC D in 6%. Three patients also underwent superficial femoral artery (SFA) stenting; one had concomitant CFA stenting, and 24 (49%) underwent treatment distal to the CFA atherectomy site. We encountered three complications: one readmission for dehydration, one postoperative hematoma, and one focal SFA dissection requiring delayed secondary stent placement. There were no deaths within 90 days. Post-procedure, the average ABI increased from 0.59 to 0.80 (P<0.01), and toe pressure rose from 42 to 68 (P<0.01). Thirty-five cases had follow-up of at least one year, showing a primary patency rate of 86% and a 94% MALE-free at one year. Additionally, 71% reported symptom improvement or wound healing at their last follow-up. CONCLUSION: When open surgery may be medically prohibited, CFA atherectomy combined with balloon angioplasty can be performed safely, yielding good clinical outcomes as a standalone procedure or with additional infrainguinal interventions. When applied in appropriate clinical and radiologic circumstances, patients experience favorable outcomes with low procedural morbidity. Due to its clinical benefits and low risk, this procedure can be a valuable addition to the modern vascular surgeon's treatment armamentarium.

Some patients with CFA occlusive disease have significant comorbidities that may prevent them from undergoing open surgery. Several endovascular treatment options for the CFA, such as atherectomy, angioplasty, and stenting, are available but have not been widely adopted.

title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality. RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs 6.6% vs 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend= 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short- and long-term outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

title: Guideline-to-Practice Gap in Ankle-Brachial Index Screening Among Inpatients with Newly Documented Lower Extremity Wounds.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and underdiagnosed. Hospitalized patients with lower extremity wounds may represent a missed opportunity for recognition. This study described inpatient ankle-brachial index (ABI) screening patterns in this population. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to two hospitals within a single urban academic health system in 2025 with a new lower extremity wound documented in nursing wound flowsheets. Recent screening was defined as ABI testing performed during the index hospitalization or within one year prior to admission. Patient and admission characteristics were compared by screening status, and logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with screening. Wound location and noninvasive vascular testing results were summarized descriptively. RESULTS: Among 2244 inpatients with newly documented lower extremity wounds, 343 patients (15.3%) were screened with ABIs. Screened patients were younger (65 vs 69 years; P<.001) and had a higher burden of atherosclerotic or diabetic comorbidities. After multivariable adjustment, pre-existing PAD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.79; P<.001), diabetes mellitus (aOR, 2.72; P<.001), and end-stage renal disease (aOR, 1.60; P=.021) were independently associated with ABI screening. Female sex was associated with lower odds of screening (aOR, 0.73; P=.045). Compared with medicine or hospitalist services, admission to general surgery/acute care surgery (aOR, 2.15; P=.002) and vascular surgery (aOR, 4.29; P<.001) was associated with higher odds of screening. Screening proportions were 23.6% for toe wounds, 20.6% for ankle/Achilles wounds, 19.9% for foot/heel wounds, and 12.8% for lower leg wounds. Among screened patients with available measurements, 50.4% had an abnormal ABI, 63.8% had an abnormal TBI, and 69.0% had at least one abnormal ABI or TBI. CONCLUSION: PAD screening was performed in a minority of hospitalized patients with newly documented lower extremity wounds and was associated with recognized vascular risk factors and admitting service. Abnormal physiologic testing was common among screened patients. Standardized wound-triggered screening pathways may reduce missed opportunities for vascular evaluation.

title: Long-term Outcomes of Primary Femoropopliteal Stents: A Retrospective Multi-Centre Experience and the Role for a Doppler Ultrasound Surveillance Programme.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularisation is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating re-intervention, remains a challenge. This study performs a retrospective outcomes analysis to suggest which patient populations may benefit from a Doppler ultrasound (DUS) surveillance programme in improving primary patency and amputation-free survival following femoropopliteal stenting in patients with PAD. METHODS: A multicentre, retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from patients who underwent femoropopliteal stenting between January 2015 and April 2023 within a vascular network with six hospital sites. Data were collected from 238 stents in 220 patients. Demographics, stent characteristics, and surveillance protocols were analysed. Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models were used to identify risk factors for primary patency and amputation-free survival. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated for both outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to compare outcomes between supra-popliteal and infra-popliteal stents. RESULTS: A total of 238 stents were inserted in a population comprised of 28.6% females, with the median age of 72.5 +/- 11.5 years. In 74.8% (178) of cases, patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Primary patency rates at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years were 90%, 67.7%, 51.2%, 26.6%, and 11.7%, respectively. The average amputation-free survival was 3.2 years. Cox regression identified CLTI (hazard ratio, 6.37, p = .001), type 1 diabetes mellitus (hazard ratio, 3.16, p = .006), and female sex (hazard ratio, 1.69, P = .037) as significant predictors of loss of primary patency. Drug-eluting stents and diabetes were associated with poorer amputation-free survival. CONCLUSIONS: The study illustrates a cohort of high-risk patients, particularly those with CLTI and diabetes, who may benefit from future enrolment in an enhanced DUS surveillance programme targeted to improve long-term outcomes. However, further research is required to explore the clinical-effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and implementation feasibility of such programmes in clinical practice.

Endovascular revascularisation is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetes-Related Foot Disease: An Arterial-Wall Dimension Uncharacterized in Current Limb Staging.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on haemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging. METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischaemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS). RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis. An elevated ankle-brachial index is uninterpretable, and a reference-range value does not exclude peripheral artery disease. Across cohorts of differing design and definition, MAC has been consistently associated with major amputation, delayed wound healing and mortality, in line with a systematic review of 51 calcification-scoring studies; the five-point pedal score has been externally validated, and associations persisted after adjustment for WIfI stage. Model comparison in one cohort suggests incremental information, but discrimination, calibration and reclassification beyond established staging have not been reported. Neither WIfI nor GLASS characterizes arterial-wall phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: The consistency and reproducibility of the prognostic evidence justify formal consideration of MAC in forthcoming revisions of limb-staging systems and guidelines. Incremental-value analyses should accompany that evaluation and inform the form of any modifier rather than delay it. One concrete route is to use MAC as a qualifier of the reliability of the WIfI ischaemia grade in the individual limb.

METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischaemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS). RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis.

title: Five-Year Outcomes of Covered Stent-Graft Repair for Traumatic and Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Injuries.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular repair with covered stent-grafts offers a prompt and effective strategy to manage lower-extremity arterial trauma and catheterization-related iatrogenic vascular complications. However, long-term durability and late complication profiles of covered stent-grafts in the femoral segments remain poorly defined. The aim of the study was to evaluate the long-term outcomes of covered stent-grafting for traumatic and iatrogenic injuries of the common, superficial, and deep femoral arteries over a 5-year follow-up period. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 58 consecutive patients (40 males [69.0%]; mean age: 57 ± 13.6 years) who underwent endovascular repair for femoral arterial injuries between August 2011 and August 2021 were analyzed. The primary outcome was the 5-year primary patency rate. Secondary outcomes included primary-assisted and secondary patency rates, as well as subgroup comparisons of patency based on stent-graft type, lesion type, and injury type. RESULTS: Etiologies included iatrogenic injury in 36 patients (62.1%) and traumatic injury in 22 patients (37.9%). Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases. The overall 5-year Kaplan-Meier estimates for primary, primary-assisted, and secondary patency rates were 72.4%, 91.4%, and 94.8%, respectively, with a mean primary patency duration of 52 months. Log-rank tests demonstrated no statistically significant differences in primary patency rates across stent-graft types (p = 0.942), lesion types (p = 0.751), or injury types (p = 0.864). CONCLUSION: In appropriately selected patients, covered stent-graft repair was associated with high technical success, low observed complication rates, and favorable long-term patency for traumatic and iatrogenic femoral arterial injuries.

However, long-term durability and late complication profiles of covered stent-grafts in the femoral segments remain poorly defined. The aim of the study was to evaluate the long-term outcomes of covered stent-grafting for traumatic and iatrogenic injuries of the common, superficial, and deep femoral arteries over a 5-year follow-up period.

title: Brachial Plexus Injuries from Overhead Arm Positioning During F/BEVAR: A Case Series and Call for Standardized Technique.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR. DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, cohort. METHODS: All consecutive patients undergoing F/BEVAR performed with bilateral overhead arm positioning at *our* Hospital between 2023 and 2025 were included. Neutral head position, padded overhead support, and abduction limited to ≤90° were used in accordance with standardized positioning protocols. Demographic, comorbidity, and procedural data were accessed from the clinical records. The primary aim was to evaluate the rate of post-operative UES and brachial plexus injury (BPI). In cases with BPI, neurological consultation and rehabilitation outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: Among 67 patients who underwent F/BEVAR with bilateral overhead arm position, six patients (9.0%) developed postoperative UES. Two patients (3.0%) had neurologist-confirmed BPI; one developed bilateral palsy with partial recovery after 8 weeks, while the other developed unilateral palsy with complete recovery by 3 months. Neither patient required surgical intervention, The remaining four patients (6.0%) experienced minor transient UES. There was no difference in baseline parameters between patients with and without UES. Urgent repair was more frequent among patients experiencing any UES than among those without UES (50.0% vs 9.8%; p = 0.028). Both patients with BPI underwent procedures lasting >180 minutes. Procedural technical success was 98.5%, and in-hospital mortality 1.5%. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR was associated with a measurable incidence of UES. Although most symptoms were transient and resolved without intervention, clinically significant BPI occurred in a small proportion of patients despite standardized positioning. These findings support cautious and selective use of prolonged overhead arm positioning and warrant prospective evaluation of safe positioning duration and patient-related susceptibility.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR.

title: From Virtual Reality to High-Fidelity Silicone Models: A Pilot Pathway for Training Vascular Surgeons in Robotic Skills.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This pilot study evaluated the learning curve of vascular surgeons undergoing structured VR simulator training and assessed the feasibility of performing a robotic vascular anastomosis within a team lacking prior laparoscopic or robotic experience. METHODS: Three vascular surgeons completed a structured curriculum on the RobotiX Mentor VR simulator, followed by a robotic aorto-aortic bypass with a Dacron graft performed on a high-fidelity pulsatile silicone model using the da Vinci surgical system. These procedures were compared with an open-technique anastomosis performed on the same model, with outcomes assessed via the Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (OSATS), operative time, and leakage rate. RESULTS: Surgeons completed a median of 248 training sessions across 77 distinct cases to reach the 20-hour required for robotic surgery certification, with proficiency achieved after 14-19 hours of training. Robotic anastomosis was associated with lower OSATS scores (34.5 [IQR 33.25-35.375] vs 40 [IQR 40-40]; P=0.003) and longer operative times (47 [IQR 41.5-57.75] vs 12 minutes [IQR 11.0-13.75]) relative to open surgery. Leakage rates did not differ between techniques (2 mL [IQR 0-4] vs 0 mL; P=0.087), and final product quality was considered acceptable, with a median score of 23 out of 25. CONCLUSION: Vascular surgeons without prior robotic or laparoscopic experience were able to acquire basic robotic vascular anastomosis skills through a structured curriculum combining VR and high-fidelity silicone simulation. Despite longer operative times relative to open surgery, technical quality and leakage rates were comparable between techniques.

title: Generalist vascular training in a subspecialising specialty: operative exposure and workforce implications from a national UK vascular surgery eLogbook analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Vascular surgery became a standalone specialty in the United Kingdom (UK) in 2012, breaking away from general surgery, with trainees completing a 6-year Higher Specialty Training (HST) programme to attain a Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT) in vascular surgery. Operative exposure in this new training programme and time to CCT remain poorly described, with implications for workforce planning and training structure. METHODS: A retrospective observational analysis of anonymised eLogbook data was performed for all National Training Number holders awarded CCT in vascular surgery between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024. Data were obtained from the Joint Committee on Surgical Training and mapped to ten portfolio index procedural categories. RESULTS: Thirty-six trainees achieved CCT during the study period. Fewer than half completed within the planned 6-year duration (median 6.75 years, IQR 6-8.63). In total, 48 636 operative cases were logged, and median active operative participation was 1 000 cases per trainee(IQR 901 - 1 161). Major and minor amputations, alongside debridement formed the largest index category (192 cases, IQR 138 - 232); vascular access surgery was the lowest (38 cases, IQR 21 - 72). When AAA repair was considered as two distinct procedures, median exposure for both open and endovascular repair fell below that of vascular access surgery. CONCLUSIONS: Training duration routinely exceeds the nominal 6-year pathway, with implications for workforce supply modelling. Operative exposure is unevenly distributed, raising questions about the adequacy of a generalist training model in a subspecialising specialty and the role of targeted post-CCT fellowship provision.

Operative exposure in this new training programme and time to CCT remain poorly described, with implications for workforce planning and training structure. METHODS: A retrospective observational analysis of anonymised eLogbook data was performed for all National Training Number holders awarded CCT in vascular surgery between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024.

title: Comparative Perioperative Outcomes of Rescue FEVAR vs Open Repair for Failed EVAR.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Redo aortic repair following previous endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is often technically challenging and associated with significant morbidity. Technologic advances in custom modified grafts have permitted increased utilization of endovascular versus open repairs. Despite this progress, there is limited data surrounding the comparative perioperative outcomes between these procedural approaches. METHODS: The National Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients undergoing elective open abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair or fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) with a physician-modified (PMEG) or custom graft (CMD) following a previous EVAR from 2010 to 2024. A univariate analysis to compare groups was completed with chi square and Fisher's Exact T-test, and outcomes were compared using multivariate logistic and linear regression. Data was analyzed using STATA. RESULTS: 900 patients underwent open repair, and 651 patents underwent FEVAR following previous EVAR. Using multivariate linear regression, patients undergoing open repair had an increased risk of postoperative pneumonia (OR 6.23, p=0.001), postoperative reintubation (OR 2.01, p=0.005), and major adverse cardiac events (OR 2.16, p=0.001) compared to patients undergoing FEVAR. Patients undergoing open repair had a higher risk of mortality (OR 2.02, p=0.018) and were less likely to be discharged home (OR 0.47, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Complex endovascular rescue of previously failed EVAR is associated with decreased the rate of perioperative complications compared to an open approach. FEVAR utilizing PMEG or CMD may be considered as a viable option in patients who are undergoing elective redo AAA repair following a failed EVAR.

Technologic advances in custom modified grafts have permitted increased utilization of endovascular versus open repairs. Despite this progress, there is limited data surrounding the comparative perioperative outcomes between these procedural approaches.
