title: Long-Term Patency and Clinical Outcomes After Retrograde Mesenteric Bypass for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centres, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass. METHODS: We evaluated 34 patients treated with retrograde mesenteric bypass for CMI between 2009 and 2024. Patency rates were measured with Kaplan-Meier analysis. Thrombosis was classified as early (≤30 days), mid-term (31-365 days), or late (>365 days). RESULTS: Superior mesenteric artery bypass was performed in 33 patients (97.1%), celiac bypass in 25 (73.5%), and dual-vessel reconstruction in 24 (70.6%). Median follow-up was 2737 days (IQR, 1760-4353), approximately 7.5 years. No early thrombosis occurred. Two mid-term and three late occlusions were observed. Primary patency rates were 93.3% at 1 and 3 years, 89.4% at 5 years, and 85.0% at 10 years. Clinical symptoms resolved after revascularisation in all patients surviving the perioperative period, and no recurrent symptoms were documented during follow-up. No patient required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Retrograde mesenteric bypass was associated with stable long-term patency, sustained symptom resolution, and low perioperative mortality. It remains a durable open surgical option for chronic mesenteric ischemia, particularly when endovascular revascularisation is not feasible or is unlikely to provide durable results.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centres, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass.

title: A Scoping Review on Artificial Intelligence for Image-Based Analysis in Aortic Aneurysm Care.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance automated image analysis, quantitative assessment, and clinical decision-making in aortic aneurysm care. This scoping review aims to summarize the current cumulative body of evidence. METHODS: A systematic PubMed search identified 661 records, with 59 studies ultimately included after de-duplication and multi-stage screening based on predefined eligibility criteria, focusing on original research applying artificial intelligence to medical imaging in aortic aneurysm care. Data were extracted on study design, imaging modality, AI methodology, validation, and dataset characteristics. RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Deep learning approaches, particularly U-Net-based architectures, were the most frequently applied methods, with AI primarily used for automated segmentation and quantitative analysis of aortic pathology. AI models achieved high technical performance across applications, including vessel segmentation, aneurysm detection, endoleak identification, and risk prediction, with reported improvements in efficiency and diagnostic accuracy. However, external validation, multimodal data integration, and prospective clinical evaluation remained uncommon. CONCLUSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential to enhance aortic aneurysm disease assessment through accurate image analysis, automated quantification, and improved procedural support. However, current limitations include lack of external validation, reporting transparency, and clinical integration.

title: Impact of Angiographic Lesion Distribution on Walking Therapy Outcomes in Lower Extremity Artery Disease.
abstract: AIM: To investigate whether angiographic lesion distribution and disease severity influence outcomes of walking therapy in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) and intermittent claudication (IC). METHODS: In this prospective, single-center cohort study, patients with IC participated in a 12-week hybrid progressive walking program consisting of one supervised treadmill session and two home-based walking sessions per week. Baseline evaluation included assessment of ankle-brachial index (ABI), angiographic imaging (CTA or MRA), and functional exercise testing. Pain-free walking distance (PFWD) and maximal walking distance (MWD) were assessed using standardized treadmill protocols. Angiographic lesion distribution was classified according to lesion location, while disease severity was graded using the ANGIO score. RESULTS: Thirty-three patients (mean age 69.1 ± 9.4 years, 75.8% male) with available angiographic imaging were included in the present analysis. After three months, PFWD increased from 173 m to 304 m, an increase of 131 m (p < 0.001), and MWD increased from 448 m to 627 m, an increase of 179 m (p < 0.001). Lesion distribution was not significantly associated with changes in PFWD (p = 0.059), and no statistically significant differences were observed for MWD (p = 0.44). Disease severity, expressed by the ANGIO score, was not correlated with walking improvements (ρ = -0.10, p = 0.57 for PFWD; ρ = 0.10, p = 0.56 for MWD). CONCLUSION: Walking therapy significantly improved walking capacity in patients with LEAD. In this exploratory cohort, no statistically significant associations were observed between angiographic lesion distribution or disease severity and improvements in walking distance. However, the small overall sample size and limited number of patients within several lesion distribution groups preclude firm conclusions regarding the influence of lesion characteristics on treatment response. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in larger studies.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center cohort study, patients with IC participated in a 12-week hybrid progressive walking program consisting of one supervised treadmill session and two home-based walking sessions per week. Baseline evaluation included assessment of ankle-brachial index (ABI), angiographic imaging (CTA or MRA), and functional exercise testing.

title: One-Year Sac Regression After Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Is Not Always Associated With Favorable Outcomes.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after EVAR indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression. METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent non-ruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020. All patients were stratified into three groups based on their 1-year sac behavior: sac regression (decrease in diameter of ≥ 5mm), stable sac (<5mm change), and sac expansion (increase in diameter of ≥ 5mm). The primary outcome was late re-intervention, including endovascular re-intervention and open conversion. RESULTS: A total of 317 patients were enrolled based on sac status on 1-year follow-up imaging: 126 with sac regression, 177 with stable sacs, and 14 with sac expansion. Over a median follow-up of 69.5 months, sac expansion was a significant risk factor for late re-intervention compared to sac regression (HR, 2.335; 95% CI, 1.048 - 5.191; P=0.047). However, the rate of late re-intervention was not significantly lower in the sac regression group compared to the stable sac group (HR, 0.694; 95% CI, 0.383 - 1.258; P=0.229). Among patients with sac regression at 1 year, 5.6% (7/126) required embolization due to endoleak, and 3.2% (4/126) needed open conversions. CONCLUSION: Late re-intervention rates did not differ significantly between patients with stable versus regressed sacs at 1 year. Patients with sac regression also require regular imaging surveillance to detect late complications.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after EVAR indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression. METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent non-ruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020.

title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins After Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n=120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n=13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors. RESULTS: Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (IQR, 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap CI, 2.2-3.7; p<0.001). Completion DUS confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; p=0.015). CONCLUSIONS: Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n=120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n=13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months.

title: Antiplatelet Therapy and Bleeding, Thrombosis, and Aneurysm Growth in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with AAAs, but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs. METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed. Demographics and outcomes were compared by antiplatelet status, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with mortality, MACE, bleeding, and AAA growth. RESULTS: Among 886 (73% male) patients studied, 511 (57.7%) were prescribed antiplatelet therapy. Those prescribed antiplatelet therapy had higher rates of atherosclerotic disease than those not on antiplatelets. Patients not prescribed antiplatelet therapy were more likely to be female, have atrial fibrillation, and be prescribed anticoagulation. At a mean follow-up of 1.8 years, there were no differences in bleeding, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism events, or growth rate associated with antiplatelet prescription. Adjusted analyses showed statins (HR=0.73, p=0.02), but not antiplatelets or anticoagulants, were associated with reduced risk of mortality. Diabetes was associated with decreased AAA growth rate, while larger initial diameter was associated with increased growth rate as well as mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with AAA, antiplatelet therapy was not observed to be associated with an increase in bleeding risk, but was also not associated with decreased mortality, thrombosis, or aneurysm growth. Statins were observed to be associated with reduced mortality. Aneurysmal growth rate was not associated with any medical therapies studied, including statins, and was only influenced by the presence of diabetes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with AAAs, but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs. METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed.

title: Early and midterm outcomes of the Gore Excluder Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis within and outside the instructions for use for aortoiliac and iliac artery aneurysms.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate perioperative and midterm outcomes of endovascular aneurysm repair using the Gore Excluder Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis (IBE) for aortoiliac and iliac artery aneurysms treated within and outside the instructions for use (IFU). METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent IBE implantation for non-ruptured aortoiliac or iliac artery aneurysms between April 2017 and December 2022. Outcomes were analyzed at the patient, procedure, or IBE-treated-side level, as appropriate. The primary endpoints were technical success, IBE-related complications, and reinterventions. Secondary endpoints included internal iliac artery (IIA) branch patency, aneurysm sac status, and freedom from reintervention or aneurysm-related death. RESULTS: A total of 56 unique patients underwent 58 procedures involving 73 IBE-treated sides; 24 sides were within-IFU and 49 were outside-IFU. Technical success was achieved in 100% of within-IFU procedures and 95.0% of outside-IFU procedures. At 36 months, freedom from reintervention was 79.1% and 94.0% in the within-IFU and outside-IFU groups, respectively (P = .24), and IIA branch patency was 88.8% and 85.5%, respectively. No significant between-group difference in IIA branch patency was detected after accounting for within-patient clustering (hazard ratio, 1.53; 95% confidence interval, 0.28-8.35; P = .62). Seven IIA branch occlusions occurred during follow-up, none of which was associated with buttock claudication. In exploratory univariable analysis, type II endoleak was associated with CIA aneurysm sac growth (odds ratio, 7.86; 95% confidence interval, 1.08-57.0; P = .04). CONCLUSIONS: IBE use outside the IFU was feasible in carefully selected patients. No significant differences in midterm clinical outcomes were detected between the within-IFU and outside-IFU groups.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent IBE implantation for non-ruptured aortoiliac or iliac artery aneurysms between April 2017 and December 2022. Outcomes were analyzed at the patient, procedure, or IBE-treated-side level, as appropriate.

title: Long-term outcomes after angioarchitecture-based endovascular treatment of cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center cohort study from Germany.
abstract: PURPOSE: Endovascular treatment is an established option for cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs), and its efficacy has been demonstrated in single-center and multicenter cohorts. In this study, we critically evaluate our single-center experience with a standardized endovascular treatment strategy, assessing angiographic success, recurrence, safety, and long-term outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients treated endovascularly for cranial dAVFs from January 2014 to October 2019 at the Institute for Neuroradiology, University Hospital Frankfurt, Germany; direct carotid-cavernous fistulas were excluded. Fistulas were Cognard-classified, cavernous-sinus dAVFs additionally Barrow-classified. Treatment was based on angioarchitecture and accessibility, using transarterial liquid embolization and/or transvenous coils. Outcomes included angiographic success, complications, recurrence/retreatment, and symptom evolution from records, follow-up, and structured telephone interviews; median patient-reported clinical follow-up was 53 months. RESULTS: Fifty-five patients were included. Cognard I/ IIa/ IIa + b/ IIb/ III/ IV/ V distribution was 6/10/1/13/16/8/1; 39/55 were high-grade. Definite venous/sinus thrombosis was documented in 22. Initial hemorrhage occurred in 9 and was associated with high-risk drainage (8/22 vs 1/33; p=0.0017) and high-grade Cognard lesions (9/39 vs 0/16; p=0.046). Embolization achieved complete occlusion in 49 cases; three additional patients had residual Cognard type I shunting, resulting in angiographic success in 52/55 patients. One recurrence, three clinical complications, and one technical complication occurred. Patient-reported improvement occurred in 46/50; tinnitus improved most, whereas diplopia persisted in 2/6 cases. CONCLUSION: This single-center study provides a real-world evaluation of our institutional treatment strategy. Our findings support its feasibility, while the small, heterogeneous cohort limits broader conclusions regarding treatment efficacy and durability.

In this study, we critically evaluate our single-center experience with a standardized endovascular treatment strategy, assessing angiographic success, recurrence, safety, and long-term outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients treated endovascularly for cranial dAVFs from January 2014 to October 2019 at the Institute for Neuroradiology, University Hospital Frankfurt, Germany; direct carotid-cavernous fistulas were excluded.

title: Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss and Perioperative Transfusion are Independently Associated with Postoperative Morbidity and Mortality After Lower Extremity Bypass.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion. RESULTS: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 1.26, 95% CI [1.01, 1.59]), myocardial infarction (AOR 1.88, 95% CI [1.48, 2.39]), stroke (AOR 1.58, 95% CI [1.09, 2.29]), and the composite outcome (AOR 1.51, 95% CI [1.29, 1.78]). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (AOR 2.46, 95% CI [1.95, 3.10]), myocardial infarction (AOR 6.57, 95% CI [5.26, 8.21]), stroke (AOR 2.75, 95% CI [1.84, 4.12]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.08, 95% CI [3.48, 4.78]). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 2.54, 95% CI [2.09, 3.08]), myocardial infarction (AOR 7.39, 95% CI [6.08, 8.98]), stroke (AOR 3.79, 95% CI [2.76, 5.21]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.42, 95% CI [3.87, 5.05]). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion. CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

title: Carotid Endarterectomy Versus Trans-Carotid Artery Revascularisation (TCAR) for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials (CREST-2) suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach. METHODS: The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/Medline, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy", "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR". Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software. RESULTS: The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR. CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system.

title: Vascular Surgery is Overrepresented by Multiple Medical Societies Compared to its Peers.
abstract: Medical societies play an important role in representing physicians and their interests. Our objective was to compare the number, size, and fiscal strength of vascular societies compared to other cardiovascular specialties. All information was found via a systematic Internet search and with publicly available data (i.e. www.aamc.org). Medical societies representing vascular surgery (VS), cardiology (CARD), cardiothoracic surgery (CTS), and interventional radiology (IR) in the United States were compared. Board-certified physicians (www.abms.org) and publicly available financial information were tabulated (www.ProPublica.org). Board-certified vascular surgeons (n=4464) can choose to join 30 VS societies (4 national, 10 regional, 12 city/state, 4 other). In comparison, 12 societies (2 national) represent CTS (n=5869) and 16 (1 national) represent IR (n=4032) physicians. Cardiologists (n=22843) are represented by 14 (5 national) societies and an additional 27 chapters of a parent national society. The available number of vascular surgeons per national society is markedly lower than comparative specialties. Vascular societies generated $23M in revenue compared to $52M for CTS, $6M for IR, and $1.03B for CARD. CARD societies have 93% of total revenue for these four specialties and 52 times the revenues compared to VS societies. Compared to similar specialties, VS has few surgeons, yet a high number of medical societies. This segmentation may dilute the educational, governmental, societal, and patient advocacy impact of VS compared to its peers.

title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular-access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB, n=72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n=91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis. RESULTS: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P<0.001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, while a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P<0.001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P<0.001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs. 35%, P=0.002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation. CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.

We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular-access clinical follow-up database.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared. RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

title: From receptor architecture to outcome maturity: a clinical framework for multiorgan incretin therapy.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To propose a clinically usable framework that separates receptor architecture and metabolic potency from the maturity of patient-relevant outcome evidence for incretin-based therapies. METHODS: This Commentary draws on recent cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, peripheral artery disease, liver, and emerging polyagonist evidence to define outcome maturity across five domains: endpoint directness and clinical relevance; study design and evidentiary confidence; comparator and population context; follow-up duration, durability, and safety; and molecule-, dose-, and indication-specific applicability. RESULTS: Four qualitative states of outcome evidence are proposed: preliminary, emerging, established, and mature. These categories apply to a specific molecule, dose, indication, phenotype, and outcome question and are intentionally nonnumeric. Outcome maturity does not measure treatment-effect magnitude or comparative drug efficacy. A six-step clinical workflow links the dominant organ-risk phenotype, clinically meaningful outcome, evidence maturity, applicability, treatment sustainability, and proportionate clinical positioning. CONCLUSION: Receptor architecture defines biological potential, whereas outcome maturity characterizes the directness, robustness, durability, and applicability of clinical evidence. Clinical positioning should remain proportional to phenotype-specific evidence and should not convert differences between nonaligned trials into cross-trial efficacy rankings.

METHODS: This Commentary draws on recent cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, peripheral artery disease, liver, and emerging polyagonist evidence to define outcome maturity across five domains: endpoint directness and clinical relevance; study design and evidentiary confidence; comparator and population context; follow-up duration, durability, and safety; and molecule-, dose-, and indication-specific applicability. title: [Saccular Aneurysm of the Left Extracranial Internal Carotid Artery].
abstract: Aneurysms of the extracranial carotid arteries are rare. A distinction is made between true aneurysms and pseudoaneurysms. Pulsatile swelling in the neck area and/or variable neurological symptoms can be diagnostically indicative. A distal aneurysm may be overlooked in vascular ultrasound. Diagnosis using CTA or MRA is essential for planning treatment management. Open surgical treatment is the method of choice, consisting of resection followed by vascular reconstruction or patch plasty. Endovascular methods are still decided on a case-by-case basis.

title: Artificial intelligence-based surrogate modeling of hemodynamic indicators in abdominal aortic aneurysms using computational fluid dynamics.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive dilatative disease of the abdominal aorta with high rupture-related mortality, emphasizing the need for early risk assessment. Conventional anatomical indicators, such as maximum diameter, are insufficient to characterize rupture risk, motivating the incorporation of hemodynamic parameters. Image-based CFD enables the estimation of these parameters but remains clinically limited by high computational cost and long processing times. To overcome these limitations, deep learning-based surrogate models such as MultiViewUNet have recently been proposed, though previous studies were constrained by relatively low spatial resolution and limited coverage of hemodynamic parameters. In this study, we propose MH-UNet, a multi-view, high-resolution surrogate modeling framework that extends the original MultiViewUNet to a higher input resolution and additional hemodynamic parameters. MH-UNet converts three-dimensional AAA geometries into two-dimensional images from multiple viewing angles and predicts TAWSS, OSI, RRT, and ECAP using data from 101 patients. Both single-inference and dual-inference strategies were implemented and compared. Single-inference consistently outperformed dual-inference across all parameters; the cascaded dual-inference scheme amplified errors through the nonlinear OSI and RRT formulations, resulting in negative R² values for OSI, RRT, and ECAP. Among the single-inference predictions, TAWSS was predicted most reliably (R² = 0.803), whereas OSI was the most challenging to predict. Agreement between single-inference predictions and CFD-derived results demonstrates the potential of MH-UNet as a rapid surrogate tool for estimating WSS-derived hemodynamic indices in AAA under fixed boundary conditions.

Image-based CFD enables the estimation of these parameters but remains clinically limited by high computational cost and long processing times.

title: Emergency thoracoabdominal aortic repair: distal-first approach with two previous aortic repairs.
abstract: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair after prior endovascular intervention is among the most technically demanding procedures in aortic surgery. We present an emergency thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair in a 59-year-old man with a history of preoperative haemodialysis, previous frozen elephant trunk for acute type A aortic dissection, followed by thoracic endovascular stent graft, complicated by partial spinal cord ischaemia and a type Ib endoleak. He presented with chest pain, and imaging demonstrated a 74 mm descending thoracic aortic aneurysm with impending rupture features. Multidisciplinary consensus deemed further endovascular intervention unsuitable, necessitating emergency open repair. A distal-first approach was used to overcome the distal perfusion challenges imposed by chronic aortic dissection. Following infrarenal clamping and the distal anastomosis to a branched graft, left heart bypass was established through its sidearm. Sequential visceral perfusion was performed, followed by anastomosis of the right renal and coeliac arteries to the graft branches. The proximal anastomosis incorporated both frozen elephant trunk and thoracic endovascular aortic repair, reinforced with double Teflon strips. The intercostal arteries were reimplanted. After declamping and de-airing, the superior mesenteric and left renal arteries were anastomosed. Motor-evoked potentials and cerebral monitoring were preserved. The patient recovered well and was discharged home 5 weeks postoperatively with a patent repair on imaging.

title: Benefits of surgical task trainers to complement training pathways for junctional haemorrhage control.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Junctional haemorrhage remains a recognised cause of preventable trauma mortality. Although uncommon in the United Kingdom, such injuries demand prompt haemorrhage control, open vascular exposure and temporary shunting. Opportunities to develop these skills during routine vascular training are limited. This study evaluated whether high-fidelity pulsatile bleeding simulation improved trainees' self-reported confidence in managing groin junctional haemorrhage. METHODS: A prospective pilot educational evaluation was undertaken during a South West Deanery vascular training day. Nine vascular surgery trainees (ST3-ST7) completed a simulation using the Trauma Simulation® Femoral Injury Groin Task Trainer, identifying the bleeding source, obtaining proximal and distal femoral control, and inserting a temporary shunt under pulsatile haemorrhage. Confidence across four procedural domains was rated on a 5-point Likert scale immediately before and after the exercise, and scores compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank testing. No objective performance assessment was undertaken. RESULTS: n p All nine trainees completed both questionnaires. Median confidence improved in all four domains, although whole-cohort changes were not statistically significant. Among junior trainees (ST3-ST6, = 6), improvements in haemorrhage management, proximal and distal vascular control, and shunt insertion were significant (all < 0.05). The three ST7 trainees showed smaller changes; the groups were not compared statistically. Participants highlighted the realism of pulsatile haemorrhage and the value of consultant-led debriefing. CONCLUSIONS: High-fidelity pulsatile bleeding simulation is feasible, was valued by trainees and may help address an experiential gap in UK vascular training. However, confidence is not competence, and objective performance measures are needed before wider curricular adoption.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Junctional haemorrhage remains a recognised cause of preventable trauma mortality. Although uncommon in the United Kingdom, such injuries demand prompt haemorrhage control, open vascular exposure and temporary shunting. Opportunities to develop these skills during routine vascular training are limited.

title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage.

title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen. SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve.

title: A re-tightening suture technique for hemostasis during aortic root remodeling in chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection.
abstract: We report a 45-year-old man with chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection, a sinus of Valsalva aneurysm, and severe aortic regurgitation. His atopic dermatitis remained poorly controlled despite topical corticosteroids and injectable anti-inflammatory therapy and he occasionally experienced cutaneous bleeding from unconscious scratching during sleep. He therefore wished to avoid long-term anticoagulation. Valve-sparing root replacement using root remodeling with external annuloplasty was performed. Bleeding from the proximal continuous suture line was controlled using a re-tightening suture technique that lifted the bleeding point, facilitated placement of an additional mattress suture, and secured the redundant continuous suture under renewed tension. Postoperative imaging showed satisfactory root geometry and no residual aortic regurgitation. This technique may provide a simple and reproducible method for controlling difficult suture-line bleeding during root remodeling.

title: Orthotopic heart transplantation associated with hemiarch reconstruction for advanced heart failure and chronic aortic dissection: a case report.
abstract: Concomitant orthotopic heart transplantation and aortic arch replacement are extremely rare, particularly in chronic Stanford type A dissection. A 43-year-old man with end-stage heart failure and chronic aortic dissection underwent combined orthotopic heart transplantation and hemiarch replacement. Because of concomitant liver donation, the donor inferior vena cava required pericardial patch reconstruction. Despite early right ventricular dysfunction requiring veno-arterial ECMO, the patient recovered completely and was discharged with preserved graft function. This case demonstrates the feasibility of a single-stage combined approach with excellent postoperative outcomes in carefully selected patients.

title: Development and Clinical Validation of a Stroke Risk Decision System for Patients With Carotid Artery Plaque Based on AI-Powered Handheld Ultrasound and Laboratory Markers.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a fusion model combining portable artificial intelligence (AI) ultrasound imaging with multidimensional laboratory data to stratify risk and support decision-making in patients with carotid plaque-related anterior circulation stroke, and to assess its predictive performance and clinical utility. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded. All participants completed the 180-day follow-up. The primary outcome was new-onset anterior circulation stroke or TIA, defined as focal neurological deficit > 24 h with CT/MRI-confirmed infarction, or transient (< 24 h) deficit without evidence of acute infarction on neuroimaging. Outcomes were adjudicated by two neurologists (attending or above), with a third for disagreements. Participants were classified into ACS group (n = 140) and non-ACS group (n = 499). Ultrasound features of carotid plaques and clinical laboratory data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with ACS, and a nomogram was constructed based on the regression model. Internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap method. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (C-index and area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis [DCA] and clinical impact curves [CIC]). RESULTS: (1) Significant differences were observed between the two groups in history of hypertension, smoking, hyperlipidemia, stroke, and myocardial infarction (MI), as well as plasma triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels, carotid plaque thickness, plaque area, plaque echogenicity percentage, degree of carotid stenosis, plaque continuity score, and plaque mutability score (p < 0.05). No significant differences were found in sex, history of diabetes, total cholesterol (TC), plaque location, or plaque fibrous cap continuity analysis score (p > 0.05) (2) Multivariable logistic regression identified history of stroke, history of myocardial infarction, plaque thickness, LDL, and HDL as independent predictors of stroke. A nomogram based on these factors demonstrated good discrimination (C-index/AUC = 0.884), with a sensitivity of 84.29% and specificity of 72.55%, along with excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p = 0.250). Decision curve analysis showed superior net benefit across a range of risk thresholds compared with the null model, supporting a multi-threshold stratified intervention strategy. Notably, when the predicted risk exceeded 75%, the model's predictions closely aligned with observed outcomes. CONCLUSION: The stroke risk decision system developed using AI-powered handheld ultrasound and laboratory indicators demonstrates clinical applicability for early prediction of anterior circulation ischemic stroke and is particularly suitable for early screening and risk stratification of high-risk stroke populations in resource-limited settings.

METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded.

title: Arthroplasty After Hemophilia Gene Therapy: Perioperative Implications and Clinical Experience.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gene therapy can provide sustained endogenous factor VIII (FVIII) or factor IX (FIX) expression, creating a perioperative phenotype that differs from both conventionally treated severe hemophilia and routine arthroplasty patients. Evidence for major joint replacement after gene therapy remains limited. AIM: To synthesize current clinical evidence on arthroplasty after hemophilia gene therapy and define practical implications for hemostatic management, venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary planning. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and reference lists were searched through September 2026 for direct arthroplasty reports, invasive-procedure studies after gene therapy, and current guidance relevant to surgery and thromboprophylaxis. RESULTS: Published evidence includes dedicated total knee and total hip arthroplasty reports, trial-level arthroplasty observations, and broader invasive-procedure datasets after valoctocogene roxaparvovec, etranacogene dezaparvovec, and fidanacogene elaparvovec. These data show that gene therapy may substantially reduce exogenous factor requirements, but they do not establish a validated FVIII or FIX threshold for arthroplasty. Current World Federation of Hemophilia guidance recommends achieving procedure-appropriate factor levels, with supplemental clotting factor concentrate when necessary. In patients whose factor activity has shifted toward mild-deficiency or nonhemophilic levels, standard arthroplasty VTE-prevention principles should not be withheld solely because of the historical diagnosis of hemophilia. CONCLUSION: Arthroplasty after hemophilia gene therapy should be managed as phenotype-based major surgery: procedure-appropriate hemostasis, immediate rescue-factor access, serial postoperative monitoring, and appropriately timed VTE prophylaxis remain essential.

Evidence for major joint replacement after gene therapy remains limited. AIM: To synthesize current clinical evidence on arthroplasty after hemophilia gene therapy and define practical implications for hemostatic management, venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary planning.

title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01073-w.

Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified.

title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Probable Loeys-Dietz Syndrome with aortic root dilatation and multiple arterial tortuosity in resource-limited setting : A case report.
abstract: Loeys-Dietz Syndrome (LDS) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder that is characterized by multisystem disorders predisposing individuals to arterial and aortic aneurysms. We present the case of a 17-year-old Bangladeshi male referred to cardiology for assessment of systemic abnormalities and cardiovascular risk. He presented with craniofacial, musculoskeletal, and cutaneous abnormalities including hypertelorism, mandibular ectopic hair, joint hypermobility with mild thoracic scoliosis, residual talipes equinovarus. He had past medical history of surgically corrected congenital anomalies. Based on clinical and radiological findings, he was diagnosed with clinically suspected Loeys-Dietz Syndrome as genetic testing was unavailable. He was managed through a multidisciplinary approach with regular follow-up. This report adds to literature on Loeys-Dietz Syndrome, emphasizing on aortic root dilatation and carotid artery tortuosity as important clinical and radiological features supporting diagnosis of LDS particularly in young patients presenting with characteristic craniofacial abnormalities or suggestive radiological findings. Early recognition and multidisciplinary management are crucial in resource-limited settings to prevent life-threatening vascular complications.

title: Age-dependent impact of diabetes on limb events and mortality in patients with peripheral artery disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial risks of limb events and mortality. Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear. METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026). Patients were stratified by diabetes status and age at PAD diagnosis (35-50 vs > 50 years). The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-extremity revascularization or major amputation. All-cause mortality was a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, interaction analyses, and propensity score overlap weighting were performed. RESULTS: P P P P Among 4538 patients aged 35-50 years at PAD diagnosis, 1902 (42%) had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 12.0 years, diabetes was independently associated with higher risks of MALE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-2.01,= .032) and mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.70,< .001). Diabetes was associated with increased MALE risk in both age groups, with no significant interaction by age (for interaction = .498). In contrast, the association between diabetes and mortality was significantly stronger in patients aged 35-50 years than in those aged >50 years (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.72-2.33 vs 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33,for interaction < .001). Excess mortality associated with diabetes emerged during longer-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with increased risks of MALE and mortality in PAD, with a stronger association with mortality among patients diagnosed before age 50. These findings identify diabetes as a marker of particularly high risk in premature PAD.

title: Stent-graft placement for an axillosubclavian artery injury in a pediatric patient: A case report.
abstract: Axillosubclavian artery injury is a rare traumatic vascular injury associated with a high mortality rate. Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented. In this report, we present the case of a pediatric patient with traumatic axillosubclavian artery injury successfully treated with stent-graft placement. A 13-year-old boy was transported to a referring hospital following a traffic accident and transferred to our emergency and critical care center. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography conducted on hospital day 2 revealed a pseudoaneurysm due to right axillosubclavian artery injury, prompting endovascular stent-graft placement. The patient was discharged on hospital day 23. Although contrast-enhanced computed tomography at 1-year after discharge confirmed severe stenosis within the stent graft, distal perfusion was maintained. Notably, no ischemic symptoms or growth disturbances were observed in the right upper limb at the 3-year follow-up. Endovascular stent-graft placement appears to be a viable treatment for axillosubclavian artery injury in selected pediatric patients, particularly adolescents.
englishSummary: Axillosubclavian artery injury is a rare traumatic vascular injury associated with a high mortality rate. Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented.

title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: 2 2 PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using Iand τ. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: Ultralow-contrast stepping digital subtraction angiography for whole-limb arterial evaluation: A case report.
abstract: Stepping digital subtraction angiography (DSA) enables whole-limb arterial assessment with a single contrast injection, and diluted contrast medium may further reduce iodine exposure. A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach. Severe right external iliac artery stenosis prompted stepping DSA before and after embolization to evaluate distal embolization. Sevenfold- and tenfold-diluted stepping DSA examinations were performed before and after embolization, respectively, using identical injection parameters (3 mL/s; 30 mL). These required 4.29 and 3.0 mL of undiluted contrast medium, respectively. Although pedal artery enhancement was reduced with tenfold dilution, image quality remained acceptable, and no obvious distal embolization was identified in the visualized arteries; however, small emboli in poorly opacified pedal branches could not be excluded with tenfold dilution. Because internal iliac artery embolization was not expected to significantly alter lower-extremity arterial perfusion, the observed difference in image quality was considered to primarily reflect the difference between the two dilution protocols rather than changes in arterial hemodynamics. Ultralow-contrast stepping DSA may be a contrast-saving technique in selected cases when repeated whole-limb arterial evaluation is required.

A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach.

title: Early outcomes of the Octapro balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve in an unrestricted cohort of patients with aortic valve stenosis: the MyPro registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on early outcomes of the novel balloon-expandable (BE) Octapro transcatheter heart valve (THV) in real-world practice are limited. We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled. Primary endpoints were VARC-3 technical success, device success, and early safety at 30-day. RESULTS: 2 A total of 303 patients were included (age 78.9 ± 7.4 years; bicuspid 13%). VARC-3 technical success was 97%, peri-procedural mortality 0.3% while no procedural stroke or myocardial infarction were reported. In-hospital guidelines-indicated permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rate was 13.5%. At discharge mean gradient was 8.4 ± 4.5 mmHg, effective orifice area 1.8 ± 0.3 cm, while moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak was reported in 3.3% of the patients. At 30-day, device success was 92.4% and early safety 80%. All-cause mortality was 2.6%, stroke 0.3%, and guidelines-indicated PPI 14.2%. Mean gradient remained low (9 ± 4 mmHg). Implantation depth and baseline right bundle branch block (RBBB) were independent predictors of PPI. ROC analysis identified an implantation depth threshold of 4.75 mm associated with increased PPI risk. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world registry, the Octapro THV demonstrated high procedural success, favourable early clinical outcomes, and excellent haemodynamic performance. Implantation depth and baseline RBBB were independent predictors of PPI, supporting optimization of implantation technique to mitigate conduction disturbances.

We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled.

title: Transcatheter mitral valve implantation in complex anatomies: Outcomes after prior repair or aborted interventions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with recurrent mitral valve disease after prior repair or persistent disease following an aborted edge-to-edge repair attempt face high risks with conventional surgery. The outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve implantation (TMVI) in these distinct cohorts remain unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all patients undergoing Tendyne-TMVI between June 2020 and December 2024 for recurrent mitral valve disease after TEER, SMA, balloon valvuloplasty, or persistent mitral valve disease after aborted TEER. Outcomes were assessed using MVARC criteria. RESULTS: Of 85 TMVI procedures, 16 were included (median age 80 years (IQR 70-83); STS 6.9% (IQR 5.6-8.2)). Prior interventions were SMA (37.5%), TEER (12.5%), balloon valvuloplasty (6.2%) and aborted TEER (43.8%). Technical success was 93.8%. At discharge, all patients showed none/trace residual mitral or paravalvular regurgitation, with a mean gradient of 3.9 ± 1.1 mmHg. At 30 days, one patient presented with severe paravalvular regurgitation due to atrialization of the prosthetic valve; no stroke occurred. Acute renal failure requiring dialysis occurred in 18.8%, one major bleeding and rehospitalization for heart failure in 12.5%. Thirty-day mortality was 12.5%. NYHA class improved significantly from 3 to 2 (p = 0.042). MVARC device success at 30 days was 63%. Estimated 1- and 2-year survival was 67% and 56% with 50% of deaths being non-cardiovascular. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected high-risk patients with recurrent or persistent mitral valve disease, Tendyne TMVI achieved durable prosthetic mitral valve function, leading to significant symptomatic improvement. Failure to meet device success was mainly driven by mean mitral gradients exceeding 5 mmHg.

The outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve implantation (TMVI) in these distinct cohorts remain unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all patients undergoing Tendyne-TMVI between June 2020 and December 2024 for recurrent mitral valve disease after TEER, SMA, balloon valvuloplasty, or persistent mitral valve disease after aborted TEER.

title: Long-term cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome patients with congenital heart disease: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Congenital cardiac anomalies are a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome (TS), yet long-term cardiovascular outcome data remain limited. This study assessed cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, valve dysfunction, and aortic outcomes in TS patients with congenital cardiovascular defects. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 84 TS patients with congenital cardiovascular anomalies were analyzed, with follow-up between 01/1980 and 01/2025. Clinical, demographic, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic variables were reviewed; morbidity and mortality were recorded; descriptive statistics applied. RESULTS: 2 Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) was present in 40 patients (48%) and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) in 29 (35%); 19 patients (23%) had both. At last follow-up (median age 26 years, IQR 31 years), most patients were in NYHA class I (82%) and mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure were 121.7 ± 16.8 mmHg and 76.1 ± 13.1 mmHg, respectively. Sinus rhythm was present in 96% of the patients. In the BAV cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 6 patients (15%) at first registration to 17 (42.5%) at last follow-up. In the tricuspid aortic valve cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 1 patient (2.3%) to 12 (27.9%). The last mean ascending aortic diameter indexed to body surface area was 20.4 ± 4.6 mm/m. Aortic dissection occurred in 2 patients (2.7%). Ten patients died during follow-up; median age at death was 41 years (IQR: 52 years), and cardiac causes accounted for at least 50% of mortality. CONCLUSION: BAV and CoA predominated in this TS cohort. Despite generally favorable functional status among survivors, progressive valve dysfunction, aortic complications and cardiovascular mortality support lifelong structured surveillance.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Congenital cardiac anomalies are a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome (TS), yet long-term cardiovascular outcome data remain limited. This study assessed cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, valve dysfunction, and aortic outcomes in TS patients with congenital cardiovascular defects. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 84 TS patients with congenital cardiovascular anomalies were analyzed, with follow-up between 01/1980 and 01/2025.

title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. Subsequently, a nomogram model was established, which was validated via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The DVT rate was 26.0%. Old age (OR, 1.0228), high American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (OR, 2.2764), greater blood loss (OR, 1.0015), blood transfusion (OR, 2.7917) and high D-dimer levels (OR, 1.0251) were identified as independent risk factors (P<0.05), while living in cities, high hemoglobin, high prealbumin, high Barthel index and high Braden scores served as protective factors (P<0.05). The model yielded an area under the curve value of 0.837. Additionally, the calibration curve showed high accuracy, and DCA validated the favorable clinical applicability of this predictive model. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.

A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed.

title: [Primary and secondary microsurgical reconstruction in soft tissue sarcomas].
abstract: The reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection is sometimes essential to enable radical R0 resection, limb salvage, satisfactory functional outcomes and timely adjuvant treatment. In a retrospective cohort of 76 soft tissue reconstructions of the lower limbs, predominantly following external resections, wound coverage was consistently performed in a staged manner with a mean interval of 18 days; in more than half of the cases this interval was ≤14 days. A comprehensive review of the scientific literature on soft tissue reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection was conducted. Key prerequisites for maximum oncological safety and reconstructive reliability without delaying adjuvant therapy are plastic and reconstructive expertise within the sarcoma center, expedited pathological margin assessment and close collaboration with vascular surgery and radiotherapy.
